page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.14xlarge is an instance within the High Clock Speed family running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz across 56 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 160.0 GB of system memory, which provides approximately 2.86 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include bundled local storage and is configured without discrete GPUs. Persistent file systems and disk-based operational workloads depend entirely on network-attached storage. In addition, the instance provides a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With its 3.1 GHz processor clock and sub-3 GB per vCPU memory density, resource allocation is weighted toward compute capability rather than extreme memory capacity. The absence of local solid-state drives necessitates planning for network storage latency and throughput boundaries. This hardware balance suits parallel computational tasks, CI/CD compilation workloads, batch processing, and compute-intensive application tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.14xlarge is a compute-focused instance within the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor on x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at 3.1 GHz across 56 dedicated vCPUs alongside 160.0 GB of system memory, delivering 2.86 GB per core. The server configuration contains no integrated local storage or graphics accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage solutions. Network capability is anchored by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned. Offering a high CPU clock speed with a lean memory profile, ecs.hfg5.14xlarge is engineered for compute-heavy workloads where raw core frequency is prioritized over large RAM allocations or direct attached disks, such as distributed compilation pipelines, batch processing, and high-throughput application servers.
